name: Intersecting Storage Rings
notes: Per-ring beam energy (≈31 GeV) is recorded as a derived half of the sourced 62 GeV centre-of-mass energy; home.cern quotes only the collision energy.

beam_energy.note: Half of the sourced 62 GeV maximum centre-of-mass energy; home.cern does not state the per-ring energy.

cms_energy.quote: Protons circulated in opposite directions and collided with a maximum centre-of-mass energy of 62 GeV.

diameter.quote: The ISR was composed of two interlaced rings each with a diameter of 300 metres.

summary.plain: The world's first machine to collide two beams of protons head-on, built at CERN and running from 1971 to 1984. It convinced physicists that colliding hadrons could work, and it held the record for collision rate among hadron colliders until 2004.
summary.technical: Two interlaced proton storage rings, each 300 m in diameter, reaching 62 GeV centre-of-mass energy; first hadron collider, operated 1971-1984 and holder of the hadron-collider luminosity record until 2004.
